tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

The tool returns immediately without ending the turn or waiting for a reply; any reply arrives asynchronously as a new user message. Keep questions concise, self-contained, and easy to understand, using a level of detail appropriate to the user and task. The UI always allows a free-text answer, including when suggested options are provided. A preselected option is not submitted automatically.

options.description: Suggested answers, in display order. Put the recommended answer first; the first option is preselected by default. The user can select one option or enter a free-text answer. tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `gpt-6.1-sol`: Latest workhorse model for coding and everyday work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority, ultrafast.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

fork_turns.description: Parent history to inherit. Defaults to `all`; use `none` to start without parent history. Only `all` and `none` are supported.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

<multi_agent_role>You are `/root`, the primary agent in a team of agents collaborating to fulfill the user's goals.

At the start of your turn, you are the active agent.
You can spawn sub-agents to handle subtasks, and those sub-agents can spawn their own sub-agents.
All agents in the team, including the agents that you can assign tasks to, are equally intelligent and capable, and have access to the same set of tools.

You can use `spawn_agent` to create a new agent, `followup_task` to give an existing agent a new task and trigger a turn, and `send_message` to pass a message to a running agent without triggering a turn.
`send_message` calls may be read by a human, so ensure they are legible. Always put proper spaces between words and/or numbers.
Child agents can also spawn their own sub-agents.
You can decide how much context you want to propagate to your sub-agents with the `fork_turns` parameter.

You will receive messages in the analysis channel in the form:
```
Message Type: MESSAGE | FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: <recipient>
Sender: <author>
Payload:
<payload text>
```
They may be addressed as to=/root

Note that collaboration tools cannot be called from inside `functions.exec`. Call `spawn_agent`, `send_message`, `followup_task`, `wait_agent`, `interrupt_agent`, and `list_agents` only as direct tool calls using the recipient shown in their tool definitions, such as `to=functions.collaboration.spawn_agent`, since they are intentionally absent from the `functions.exec` `tools.*` namespace. Available tools in `functions.exec` are explicitly described with a `tools` namespace in the developer message.

All agents share the same directory. In detail:
- All agents have access to the same container and filesystem as you.
- All agents use the same current working directory.
- As a result, edits made by one agent are immediately visible to all other agents.

When calling `wait_agent`, prefer longer waits (minutes) to avoid busy polling.

There are 4 available concurrency slots, meaning that up to 4 agents can be active at once, including you.

Full-history forks (`fork_turns` omitted or `"all"`) inherit the parent model and reasoning effort and do not accept overrides. Only set `model` or `reasoning_effort` when explicitly requested by the user, applicable `AGENTS.md` instructions, or skill instructions; when doing so, set `fork_turns` to `"none"`.</multi_agent_role>

tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

tools.name: request_user_input
tools.description: Request user input for one to three short questions and wait for the response. This tool is only available in Plan mode.

questions.description: Questions to show the user. Prefer 1 and do not exceed 3

header.description: Short header label shown in the UI (12 or fewer chars).

options.description: Provide 2-3 mutually exclusive choices. Put the recommended option first and suffix its label with "(Recommended)". Do not include an "Other" option in this list; the client will add a free-form "Other" option automatically.

description.description: One short sentence explaining impact/tradeoff if selected.

question.description: Single-sentence prompt shown to the user.

tools.name: request_user_input_async
tools.description: Ask the user one or more questions during ongoing work. Use this tool only to request missing information, preferences, constraints, clarification, or approval. The tool returns immediately without ending the turn or waiting for a reply; any reply arrives asynchronously as a new user message. Keep questions concise, self-contained, and easy to understand, using a level of detail appropriate to the user and task. The UI always allows a free-text answer, including when suggested options are provided. A preselected option is not submitted automatically.

questions.description: One or more self-contained questions to present together, in display order.

options.description: Suggested answers, in display order. Put the recommended answer first; the first option is preselected by default. The user can select one option or enter a free-text answer. Do not include an Other option or a free-text placeholder; the UI provides free-text input automatically. Omit options for a free-text-only question.

title.description: The complete question shown to the user, including any context needed to answer it.

tools.name: clock
tools.description: Tools for reading and waiting on time.

tools.name: sleep
tools.description: Pause execution for a specified duration. The sleep ends early when new input arrives for the active turn. Returns the elapsed wall-clock time.

duration_ms.description: How long to sleep in milliseconds. Must be between 1 and 43200000.

tools.name: collaboration
tools.description: Tools for spawning and managing sub-agents.

tools.name: followup_task
tools.description: Send a follow-up task to an existing non-root target agent and trigger a turn if it is idle. If the target is already running, deliver the task promptly at message boundaries while sampling, or after the pending tool call completes.

message.description: Message text to send to the target agent.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to send a follow-up task to (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Interrupt an agent's current turn, if any, and return its previous status. The agent remains available for messages and follow-up tasks.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to interrupt (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List live agents in the current root thread tree. Optionally filter by task-path prefix.

path_prefix.description: Task-path prefix filter without a trailing slash. Omit to list all live agents.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to an existing agent. The message will be delivered promptly. Does not trigger a new turn.

message.description: Message text to queue on the target agent.

target.description: Relative or canonical task name to message (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `gpt-6.1-sol`: Latest workhorse model for coding and everyday work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority, ultrafast.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

fork_turns.description: Parent history to inherit. Defaults to `all`; use `none` to start without parent history. Only `all` and `none` are supported.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. The wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

content.text: You translate the supplied natural-language proof faithfully into Lean 4. Use the explicit project premises and any proved result in the pinned Mathlib environment. Preserve all assumptions, conclusions, equality modes and the supplied proof route. No reference answers, personal context, other tasks, shell or external services are available. Use the submit tool when the requested artifact is complete; if rejected, repair it. A strategy is advice, never an additional theorem or assumption. End this stage immediately when a submit tool reports stage_complete:true; the controller handles later stages. Within a proof stage, checked helper attempts are available through read_lean_draft. After a context reset, query its index before claiming no draft or helper exists. Helpers never become new premises. Use familiar interfaces directly; no background-note scan is required. For a relevant obstacle, select a matching local background_note_index entry and read_background_note if its details may help. Relate the actual Lean goal/context to its NL step: use the note grounds to identify a small missing application premise or transport, prove it from permitted inputs, then check the intended application. Verify actual types and conditions; a note is not a Lean proof or extra assumption. If it does not fit, continue ordinary allowed search or repair without insisting on that note or rebuilding a larger argument by default.

tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

tools.name: request_user_input
tools.description: Request user input for one to three short questions and wait for the response. This tool is only available in Plan mode.

questions.description: Questions to show the user. Prefer 1 and do not exceed 3

header.description: Short header label shown in the UI (12 or fewer chars).

options.description: Provide 2-3 mutually exclusive choices. Put the recommended option first and suffix its label with "(Recommended)". Do not include an "Other" option in this list; the client will add a free-form "Other" option automatically.

description.description: One short sentence explaining impact/tradeoff if selected.

question.description: Single-sentence prompt shown to the user.

tools.name: request_user_input_async
tools.description: Ask the user one or more questions during ongoing work. Use this tool only to request missing information, preferences, constraints, clarification, or approval. The tool returns immediately without ending the turn or waiting for a reply; any reply arrives asynchronously as a new user message. Keep questions concise, self-contained, and easy to understand, using a level of detail appropriate to the user and task. The UI always allows a free-text answer, including when suggested options are provided. A preselected option is not submitted automatically.

questions.description: One or more self-contained questions to present together, in display order.

options.description: Suggested answers, in display order. Put the recommended answer first; the first option is preselected by default. The user can select one option or enter a free-text answer. Do not include an Other option or a free-text placeholder; the UI provides free-text input automatically. Omit options for a free-text-only question.

title.description: The complete question shown to the user, including any context needed to answer it.

tools.name: clock
tools.description: Tools for reading and waiting on time.

tools.name: sleep
tools.description: Pause execution for a specified duration. The sleep ends early when new input arrives for the active turn. Returns the elapsed wall-clock time.

duration_ms.description: How long to sleep in milliseconds. Must be between 1 and 43200000.

tools.name: collaboration
tools.description: Tools for spawning and managing sub-agents.

tools.name: followup_task
tools.description: Send a follow-up task to an existing non-root target agent and trigger a turn if it is idle. If the target is already running, deliver the task promptly at message boundaries while sampling, or after the pending tool call completes.

message.description: Message text to send to the target agent.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to send a follow-up task to (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Interrupt an agent's current turn, if any, and return its previous status. The agent remains available for messages and follow-up tasks.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to interrupt (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List live agents in the current root thread tree. Optionally filter by task-path prefix.

path_prefix.description: Task-path prefix filter without a trailing slash. Omit to list all live agents.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to an existing agent. The message will be delivered promptly. Does not trigger a new turn.

message.description: Message text to queue on the target agent.

target.description: Relative or canonical task name to message (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `gpt-6.1-sol`: Latest workhorse model for coding and everyday work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority, ultrafast.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

fork_turns.description: Parent history to inherit. Defaults to `all`; use `none` to start without parent history. Only `all` and `none` are supported.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. The wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

content.text: You translate the supplied natural-language proof faithfully into Lean 4. Use the explicit project premises and any proved result in the pinned Mathlib environment. Preserve all assumptions, conclusions, equality modes and the supplied proof route. No reference answers, personal context, other tasks, shell or external services are available. Use the submit tool when the requested artifact is complete; if rejected, repair it. A strategy is advice, never an additional theorem or assumption. End this stage immediately when a submit tool reports stage_complete:true; the controller handles later stages. Within a proof stage, checked helper attempts are available through read_lean_draft. After a context reset, query its index before claiming no draft or helper exists. Helpers never become new premises. Use familiar interfaces directly; no background-note scan is required. For a relevant obstacle, select a matching local background_note_index entry and read_background_note if its details may help. Relate the actual Lean goal/context to its NL step: use the note grounds to identify a small missing application premise or transport, prove it from permitted inputs, then check the intended application. Verify actual types and conditions; a note is not a Lean proof or extra assumption. If it does not fit, continue ordinary allowed search or repair without insisting on that note or rebuilding a larger argument by default.

tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

25:     IsLocalizedModule S (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R A Aₛ).toLinearMap ↔
26:       IsLocalization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid A S) Aₛ := by

28:   refine and_congr ?_ (and_congr (forall_congr' fun _ ↦ ?_) (forall₂_congr fun _ _ ↦ ?_))

30:       Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid, ← SetLike.mem_coe, Submonoid.coe_map,
31:       Set.forall_mem_image, ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply]
32:   · simp_rw [Prod.exists, Subtype.exists, Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid]
33:     simp [← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply, Submonoid.mk_smul, Algebra.smul_def, mul_comm]
34:   · congr!; simp_rw [Subtype.exists, Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid]; simp [Algebra.smul_def]
35: 
36: instance [IsLocalization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid A S) Aₛ] :
37:     IsLocalizedModule S (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R A Aₛ).toLinearMap :=

43: the associated linear map `R →ₗ[R] A` is a localization of modules with respect to `S`. -/

tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

17: section IsLocalizedModule
18: 
19: variable {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] (S : Submonoid R)
20: variable {A Aₛ : Type*} [CommSemiring A] [Algebra R A]
21: variable [CommSemiring Aₛ] [Algebra A Aₛ] [Algebra R Aₛ] [IsScalarTower R A Aₛ]

23: variable {S} in
24: theorem isLocalizedModule_iff_isLocalization :
25:     IsLocalizedModule S (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R A Aₛ).toLinearMap ↔
26:       IsLocalization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid A S) Aₛ := by
27:   rw [isLocalizedModule_iff, isLocalization_iff]
28:   refine and_congr ?_ (and_congr (forall_congr' fun _ ↦ ?_) (forall₂_congr fun _ _ ↦ ?_))
29:   · simp_rw [← (Algebra.lmul R Aₛ).commutes, Algebra.lmul_isUnit_iff, Subtype.forall,
30:       Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid, ← SetLike.mem_coe, Submonoid.coe_map,
31:       Set.forall_mem_image, ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply]
32:   · simp_rw [Prod.exists, Subtype.exists, Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid]
33:     simp [← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply, Submonoid.mk_smul, Algebra.smul_def, mul_comm]
34:   · congr!; simp_rw [Subtype.exists, Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid]; simp [Algebra.smul_def]
35: 
36: instance [IsLocalization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid A S) Aₛ] :
37:     IsLocalizedModule S (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R A Aₛ).toLinearMap :=
38:   isLocalizedModule_iff_isLocalization.mpr ‹_›
39: 
40: variable (A)
41: 
42: /-- `A` is a localization of a commutative semiring `R` with respect to `S` iff
43: the associated linear map `R →ₗ[R] A` is a localization of modules with respect to `S`. -/
44: lemma isLocalizedModule_iff_isLocalization' :
45:     IsLocalizedModule S (Algebra.linearMap R A) ↔ IsLocalization S A := by
46:   convert! isLocalizedModule_iff_isLocalization (S := S) (A := R) (Aₛ := A)
47:   exact (Submonoid.map_id S).symm
48: 
49: instance [IsLocalization S A] : IsLocalizedModule S (Algebra.linearMap R A) :=
50:   (isLocalizedModule_iff_isLocalization' S _).mpr inferInstance

53: /-- `IsLocalization.mk'` agrees with `IsLocalizedModule.mk'`. -/
54: lemma IsLocalization.mk'_algebraMap_eq_mk' [IsLocalization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid A S) Aₛ]
55:     {x : A} {s : S} : IsLocalization.mk' Aₛ x ⟨_, Algebra.mem_algebraMapSubmonoid_of_mem s⟩ =

59:   exact IsLocalization.smul_mk'_self (m := ⟨_, _⟩)

11: /-!
12: # Equivalence between `IsLocalizedModule` and `IsLocalization`
13: -/
14: 
15: public section
16: 
17: section IsLocalizedModule
18: 
19: variable {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] (S : Submonoid R)
20: variable {A Aₛ : Type*} [CommSemiring A] [Algebra R A]
21: variable [CommSemiring Aₛ] [Algebra A Aₛ] [Algebra R Aₛ] [IsScalarTower R A Aₛ]
22: 
23: variable {S} in
24: theorem isLocalizedModule_iff_isLocalization :
25:     IsLocalizedModule S (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R A Aₛ).toLinearMap ↔
26:       IsLocalization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid A S) Aₛ := by
27:   rw [isLocalizedModule_iff, isLocalization_iff]
28:   refine and_congr ?_ (and_congr (forall_congr' fun _ ↦ ?_) (forall₂_congr fun _ _ ↦ ?_))
29:   · simp_rw [← (Algebra.lmul R Aₛ).commutes, Algebra.lmul_isUnit_iff, Subtype.forall,
30:       Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid, ← SetLike.mem_coe, Submonoid.coe_map,
31:       Set.forall_mem_image, ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply]
32:   · simp_rw [Prod.exists, Subtype.exists, Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid]
33:     simp [← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply, Submonoid.mk_smul, Algebra.smul_def, mul_comm]
34:   · congr!; simp_rw [Subtype.exists, Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid]; simp [Algebra.smul_def]
35: 
36: instance [IsLocalization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid A S) Aₛ] :
37:     IsLocalizedModule S (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R A Aₛ).toLinearMap :=
38:   isLocalizedModule_iff_isLocalization.mpr ‹_›
39: 
40: variable (A)
41: 
42: /-- `A` is a localization of a commutative semiring `R` with respect to `S` iff
43: the associated linear map `R →ₗ[R] A` is a localization of modules with respect to `S`. -/
44: lemma isLocalizedModule_iff_isLocalization' :
45:     IsLocalizedModule S (Algebra.linearMap R A) ↔ IsLocalization S A := by
46:   convert! isLocalizedModule_iff_isLocalization (S := S) (A := R) (Aₛ := A)
47:   exact (Submonoid.map_id S).symm
48: 
49: instance [IsLocalization S A] : IsLocalizedModule S (Algebra.linearMap R A) :=
50:   (isLocalizedModule_iff_isLocalization' S _).mpr inferInstance
51: 
52: variable {S A} in
53: /-- `IsLocalization.mk'` agrees with `IsLocalizedModule.mk'`. -/
54: lemma IsLocalization.mk'_algebraMap_eq_mk' [IsLocalization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid A S) Aₛ]
55:     {x : A} {s : S} : IsLocalization.mk' Aₛ x ⟨_, Algebra.mem_algebraMapSubmonoid_of_mem s⟩ =
56:       IsLocalizedModule.mk' (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R A Aₛ).toLinearMap x s := by
57:   rw [← IsLocalizedModule.smul_inj (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R A Aₛ).toLinearMap s,
58:     IsLocalizedModule.mk'_cancel', Submonoid.smul_def, ← algebraMap_smul A]
59:   exact IsLocalization.smul_mk'_self (m := ⟨_, _⟩)
60: 
61: /-- `IsLocalization.mk'` agrees with `IsLocalizedModule.mk'`. -/
62: lemma IsLocalization.mk'_eq_mk' [IsLocalization S A] (x : R) (s : S) :
63:     IsLocalization.mk' A x s = IsLocalizedModule.mk' (Algebra.linearMap R A) x s := by
64:   rw [← IsLocalizedModule.smul_inj (Algebra.linearMap R A) s, IsLocalizedModule.mk'_cancel']
65:   exact IsLocalization.smul_mk'_self
66: 
67: end IsLocalizedModule"}

tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

tools.name: request_user_input
tools.description: Request user input for one to three short questions and wait for the response. This tool is only available in Plan mode.

questions.description: Questions to show the user. Prefer 1 and do not exceed 3

header.description: Short header label shown in the UI (12 or fewer chars).

options.description: Provide 2-3 mutually exclusive choices. Put the recommended option first and suffix its label with "(Recommended)". Do not include an "Other" option in this list; the client will add a free-form "Other" option automatically.

description.description: One short sentence explaining impact/tradeoff if selected.

question.description: Single-sentence prompt shown to the user.

tools.name: request_user_input_async
tools.description: Ask the user one or more questions during ongoing work. Use this tool only to request missing information, preferences, constraints, clarification, or approval. The tool returns immediately without ending the turn or waiting for a reply; any reply arrives asynchronously as a new user message. Keep questions concise, self-contained, and easy to understand, using a level of detail appropriate to the user and task. The UI always allows a free-text answer, including when suggested options are provided. A preselected option is not submitted automatically.

questions.description: One or more self-contained questions to present together, in display order.

options.description: Suggested answers, in display order. Put the recommended answer first; the first option is preselected by default. The user can select one option or enter a free-text answer. Do not include an Other option or a free-text placeholder; the UI provides free-text input automatically. Omit options for a free-text-only question.

title.description: The complete question shown to the user, including any context needed to answer it.

tools.name: clock

tools.name: sleep

tools.name: followup_task
tools.description: Send a follow-up task to an existing non-root target agent and trigger a turn if it is idle. If the target is already running, deliver the task promptly at message boundaries while sampling, or after the pending tool call completes.

message.description: Message text to send to the target agent.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to send a follow-up task to (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Interrupt an agent's current turn, if any, and return its previous status. The agent remains available for messages and follow-up tasks.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to interrupt (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List live agents in the current root thread tree. Optionally filter by task-path prefix.

path_prefix.description: Task-path prefix filter without a trailing slash. Omit to list all live agents.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to an existing agent. The message will be delivered promptly. Does not trigger a new turn.

message.description: Message text to queue on the target agent.

target.description: Relative or canonical task name to message (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `gpt-6.1-sol`: Latest workhorse model for coding and everyday work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority, ultrafast.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

Use the submit tool when the requested artifact is complete; if rejected, repair it. A strategy is advice, never an additional theorem or assumption. Relate the actual Lean goal/context to its NL step: use the note grounds to identify a small missing application premise or transport, prove it from permitted inputs, then check the intended application. Verify actual types and conditions; a note is not a Lean proof or extra assumption. If it does not fit, continue ordinary allowed search or repair without insisting on that note or rebuilding a larger argument by default.

All agents in the team, including the agents that you can assign tasks to, are equally intelligent and capable, and have access to the same set of tools.

Child agents can also spawn their own sub-agents.

Full-history forks (`fork_turns` omitted or `"all"`) inherit the parent model and reasoning effort and do not accept overrides. 17: section IsLocalizedModule
18: 
19: variable {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] (S : Submonoid R)
20: variable {A Aₛ : Type*} [CommSemiring A] [Algebra R A]
21: variable [CommSemiring Aₛ] [Algebra A Aₛ] [Algebra R Aₛ] [IsScalarTower R A Aₛ]
22: 
23: variable {S} in
24: theorem isLocalizedModule_iff_isLocalization :
25:     IsLocalizedModule S (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R A Aₛ).toLinearMap ↔
26:       IsLocalization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid A S) Aₛ := by
27:   rw [isLocalizedModule_iff, isLocalization_iff]
28:   refine and_congr ?_ (and_congr (forall_congr' fun _ ↦ ?_) (forall₂_congr fun _ _ ↦ ?_))
29:   · simp_rw [← (Algebra.lmul R Aₛ).commutes, Algebra.lmul_isUnit_iff, Subtype.forall,
30:       Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid, ← SetLike.mem_coe, Submonoid.coe_map,
31:       Set.forall_mem_image, ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply]
32:   · simp_rw [Prod.exists, Subtype.exists, Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid]
33:     simp [← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply, Submonoid.mk_smul, Algebra.smul_def, mul_comm]
34:   · congr!; simp_rw [Subtype.exists, Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid]; simp [Algebra.smul_def]
35: 
36: instance [IsLocalization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid A S) Aₛ] :
37:     IsLocalizedModule S (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R A Aₛ).toLinearMap :=
38:   isLocalizedModule_iff_isLocalization.mpr ‹_›
39: 
40: variable (A)
41: 
42: /-- `A` is a localization of a commutative semiring `R` with respect to `S` iff
43: the associated linear map `R →ₗ[R] A` is a localization of modules with respect to `S`. -/
44: lemma isLocalizedModule_iff_isLocalization' :
45:     IsLocalizedModule S (Algebra.linearMap R A) ↔ IsLocalization S A := by
46:   convert! isLocalizedModule_iff_isLocalization (S := S) (A := R) (Aₛ := A)
47:   exact (Submonoid.map_id S).symm
48: 
49: instance [IsLocalization S A] : IsLocalizedModule S (Algebra.linearMap R A) :=
50:   (isLocalizedModule_iff_isLocalization' S _).mpr inferInstance
51: 
52: variable {S A} in
53: /-- `IsLocalization.mk'` agrees with `IsLocalizedModule.mk'`. -/
54: lemma IsLocalization.mk'_algebraMap_eq_mk' [IsLocalization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid A S) Aₛ]
55:     {x : A} {s : S} : IsLocalization.mk' Aₛ x ⟨_, Algebra.mem_algebraMapSubmonoid_of_mem s⟩ =
56:       IsLocalizedModule.mk' (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R A Aₛ).toLinearMap x s := by
57:   rw [← IsLocalizedModule.smul_inj (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R A Aₛ).toLinearMap s,
58:     IsLocalizedModule.mk'_cancel', Submonoid.smul_def, ← algebraMap_smul A]
59:   exact IsLocalization.smul_mk'_self (m := ⟨_, _⟩)
60: 
61: /-- `IsLocalization.mk'` agrees with `IsLocalizedModule.mk'`. -/
62: lemma IsLocalization.mk'_eq_mk' [IsLocalization S A] (x : R) (s : S) :
63:     IsLocalization.mk' A x s = IsLocalizedModule.mk' (Algebra.linearMap R A) x s := by
64:   rw [← IsLocalizedModule.smul_inj (Algebra.linearMap R A) s, IsLocalizedModule.mk'_cancel']
65:   exact IsLocalization.smul_mk'_self
66: 
67: end IsLocalizedModule"}

sent_payload.instructions: You translate the supplied natural-language proof faithfully into Lean 4. Use the explicit project premises and any proved result in the pinned Mathlib environment. Preserve all assumptions, conclusions, equality modes and the supplied proof route. No reference answers, personal context, other tasks, shell or external services are available. Use the submit tool when the requested artifact is complete; if rejected, repair it. A strategy is advice, never an additional theorem or assumption. End this stage immediately when a submit tool reports stage_complete:true; the controller handles later stages. Within a proof stage, checked helper attempts are available through read_lean_draft. After a context reset, query its index before claiming no draft or helper exists. Helpers never become new premises. Use familiar interfaces directly; no background-note scan is required. For a relevant obstacle, select a matching local background_note_index entry and read_background_note if its details may help. Relate the actual Lean goal/context to its NL step: use the note grounds to identify a small missing application premise or transport, prove it from permitted inputs, then check the intended application. Verify actual types and conditions; a note is not a Lean proof or extra assumption. If it does not fit, continue ordinary allowed search or repair without insisting on that note or rebuilding a larger argument by default.

tools.name: search_mathlib
tools.description: Search the pinned mathlib Lean source using a regular expression; at most 100 lines.

tools.name: read_mathlib
tools.description: Read specified lines of a Mathlib/*.lean source file from the pinned checkout.

tools.name: check_transition
tools.description: Compile a tactic body for the fixed target; no leading by, declarations, or placeholders.

tools.name: submit_transition
tools.description: Submit and check the final tactic body for the same target.

tools.name: check_auxiliary
tools.description: Compile one helper proposition and tactic body in exactly this local port context. This never accepts the final goal or adds a premise.

tools.name: read_lean_draft
tools.description: Read only your own same-stage proof/helper attempts. kind=index lists attempts; proof/auxiliary returns the selected body lines and actual check. No other stage or file is accessible.

tools.name: read_background_note
tools.description: Read one complete audited background note from this task index by its qualified ID. No other task, file or proof is accessible; this is guidance, not a checked Lean proof.

transport: Codex subscription authentication via documented custom provider

tools.name: exec

format.definition:
start: pragma_source | plain_source
pragma_source: PRAGMA_LINE NEWLINE SOURCE
plain_source: SOURCE

PRAGMA_LINE: /[ \t]*\/\/ @exec:[^\r\n]*/
NEWLINE: /\r?\n/
SOURCE: /[\s\S]+/

tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

tools.name: request_user_input
tools.description: Request user input for one to three short questions and wait for the response. This tool is only available in Plan mode.

questions.description: Questions to show the user. Prefer 1 and do not exceed 3

header.description: Short header label shown in the UI (12 or fewer chars).

options.description: Provide 2-3 mutually exclusive choices. Put the recommended option first and suffix its label with "(Recommended)". Do not include an "Other" option in this list; the client will add a free-form "Other" option automatically.

description.description: One short sentence explaining impact/tradeoff if selected.

question.description: Single-sentence prompt shown to the user.

tools.name: request_user_input_async
tools.description: Ask the user one or more questions during ongoing work. Use this tool only to request missing information, preferences, constraints, clarification, or approval. The tool returns immediately without ending the turn or waiting for a reply; any reply arrives asynchronously as a new user message. Keep questions concise, self-contained, and easy to understand, using a level of detail appropriate to the user and task. The UI always allows a free-text answer, including when suggested options are provided. A preselected option is not submitted automatically.

questions.description: One or more self-contained questions to present together, in display order.

options.description: Suggested answers, in display order. Put the recommended answer first; the first option is preselected by default. The user can select one option or enter a free-text answer. Do not include an Other option or a free-text placeholder; the UI provides free-text input automatically. Omit options for a free-text-only question.

title.description: The complete question shown to the user, including any context needed to answer it.

duration_ms.description: How long to sleep in milliseconds. Must be between 1 and 43200000.

tools.description: Interrupt an agent's current turn, if any, and return its previous status. The agent remains available for messages and follow-up tasks.

24: theorem isLocalizedModule_iff_isLocalization :
25:     IsLocalizedModule S (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R A Aₛ).toLinearMap ↔
26:       IsLocalization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid A S) Aₛ := by
27:   rw [isLocalizedModule_iff, isLocalization_iff]
28:   refine and_congr ?_ (and_congr (forall_congr' fun _ ↦ ?_) (forall₂_congr fun _ _ ↦ ?_))
29:   · simp_rw [← (Algebra.lmul R Aₛ).commutes, Algebra.lmul_isUnit_iff, Subtype.forall,
30:       Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid, ← SetLike.mem_coe, Submonoid.coe_map,
31:       Set.forall_mem_image, ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply]
32:   · simp_rw [Prod.exists, Subtype.exists, Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid]
33:     simp [← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply, Submonoid.mk_smul, Algebra.smul_def, mul_comm]
34:   · congr!; simp_rw [Subtype.exists, Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid]; simp [Algebra.smul_def]
35: 
36: instance [IsLocalization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid A S) Aₛ] :

42: /-- `A` is a localization of a commutative semiring `R` with respect to `S` iff
43: the associated linear map `R →ₗ[R] A` is a localization of modules with respect to `S`. -/
44: lemma isLocalizedModule_iff_isLocalization' :
45:     IsLocalizedModule S (Algebra.linearMap R A) ↔ IsLocalization S A := by
46:   convert! isLocalizedModule_iff_isLocalization (S := S) (A := R) (Aₛ := A)
47:   exact (Submonoid.map_id S).symm

12: /-!
13: # Localization of Submodules
14: 
15: Results about localizations of submodules and quotient modules are provided in this file.
16: 
17: ## Main results
18: - `Submodule.localized`:
19:   The localization of an `R`-submodule of `M` at `p` viewed as an `Rₚ`-submodule of `Mₚ`.
20:   A direct consequence of this is that `Rₚ` is flat over `R`; see `IsLocalization.flat`.
21: - `Submodule.toLocalized`:
22:   The localization map of a submodule `M' →ₗ[R] M'.localized p`.
23: - `Submodule.toLocalizedQuotient`:
24:   The localization map of a quotient module `M ⧸ M' →ₗ[R] LocalizedModule p M ⧸ M'.localized p`.
25: 
26: ## TODO
27: - Statements regarding the exactness of localization.
28: 
29: -/

36: variable (S) [CommSemiring R] [CommSemiring S] [AddCommMonoid M] [AddCommMonoid N]
37: variable [Module R M] [Module R N] [Algebra R S] [Module S N] [IsScalarTower R S N]
38: variable (p : Submonoid R) [IsLocalization p S] (f : M →ₗ[R] N) [IsLocalizedModule p f]

41: namespace Submodule

43: /-- Let `N` be a localization of an `R`-module `M` at `p`.
44: This is the localization of an `R`-submodule of `M` viewed as an `R`-submodule of `N`. -/
45: def localized₀ : Submodule R N where
46:   carrier := { x | ∃ m ∈ M', ∃ s : p, IsLocalizedModule.mk' f m s = x }
47:   add_mem' := fun {x y} ⟨m, hm, s, hx⟩ ⟨n, hn, t, hy⟩ ↦ ⟨t • m + s • n, add_mem (M'.smul_mem t hm)
48:     (M'.smul_mem s hn), s * t, by rw [← hx, ← hy, IsLocalizedModule.mk'_add_mk']⟩
49:   zero_mem' := ⟨0, zero_mem _, 1, by simp⟩
50:   smul_mem' r x := by
51:     rintro ⟨m, hm, s, hx⟩
52:     exact ⟨r • m, smul_mem M' _ hm, s, by rw [IsLocalizedModule.mk'_smul, hx]⟩
53: 
54: /-- Let `S` be the localization of `R` at `p` and `N` be a localization of `M` at `p`.
55: This is the localization of an `R`-submodule of `M` viewed as an `S`-submodule of `N`. -/
56: def localized' : Submodule S N where
57:   __ := localized₀ p f M'
58:   smul_mem' := fun r x ⟨m, hm, s, hx⟩ ↦ by
59:     have ⟨y, t, hyt⟩ := IsLocalization.exists_mk'_eq p r
60:     exact ⟨y • m, M'.smul_mem y hm, t * s, by simp [← hyt, ← hx, IsLocalizedModule.mk'_smul_mk']⟩
61: 
62: lemma mem_localized₀ (x : N) :
63:     x ∈ localized₀ p f M' ↔ ∃ m ∈ M', ∃ s : p, IsLocalizedModule.mk' f m s = x :=
64:   Iff.rfl
65: 
66: lemma mem_localized' (x : N) :
67:     x ∈ localized' S p f M' ↔ ∃ m ∈ M', ∃ s : p, IsLocalizedModule.mk' f m s = x :=
68:   Iff.rfl
69: 
70: /-- `localized₀` is the same as `localized'` considered as a submodule over the base ring. -/
71: lemma restrictScalars_localized' :
72:     (localized' S p f M').restrictScalars R = localized₀ p f M' :=
73:   rfl
74: 
75: theorem localized'_eq_span : localized' S p f M' = span S (f '' M') := by
76:   refine le_antisymm ?_ (span_le.mpr <| by rintro _ ⟨m, hm, rfl⟩; exact ⟨m, hm, 1, by simp⟩)
77:   rintro _ ⟨m, hm, s, rfl⟩
78:   rw [← one_smul R m, ← mul_one s, ← IsLocalizedModule.mk'_smul_mk' S]
79:   exact smul_mem _ _ (subset_span ⟨m, hm, by simp⟩)
80: 
81: theorem map_le_localized₀ : M'.map f ≤ localized₀ p f M' := by
82:   rintro - ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩
83:   rw [mem_localized₀]
84:   exact ⟨x, hx, 1, IsLocalizedModule.mk'_one p f x⟩
85: 
86: /-- The Galois insertion between `Submodule R M` and `Submodule S N`,
87: where `S` is the localization of `R` at `p` and `N` is the localization of `M` at `p`. -/
88: def localized'gi : GaloisInsertion (localized' S p f) (comap f <| ·.restrictScalars R) where
89:   gc M' N' := ⟨fun h m hm ↦ h ⟨m, hm, 1, by simp⟩, fun h ↦ by
90:     rw [localized'_eq_span, span_le]; apply map_le_iff_le_comap.mpr h⟩
91:   le_l_u N' n hn := by
92:     obtain ⟨⟨m, s⟩, rfl⟩ := IsLocalizedModule.mk'_surjective p f n
93:     refine ⟨m, ?_, s, rfl⟩
94:     rw [mem_comap, restrictScalars_mem, ← IsLocalizedModule.mk'_cancel' _ _ s,
95:       Submonoid.smul_def, ← algebraMap_smul S]
96:     exact smul_mem _ _ hn
97:   choice x _ := localized' S p f x
98:   choice_eq _ _ := rfl

100: /-- The localization of an `R`-submodule of `M` at `p` viewed as an `Rₚ`-submodule of `Mₚ`. -/
101: noncomputable abbrev localized : Submodule (Localization p) (LocalizedModule p M) :=
102:   M'.localized' (Localization p) p (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap p M)

104: @[simp]
105: lemma localized₀_bot : (⊥ : Submodule R M).localized₀ p f = ⊥ := by
106:   rw [← le_bot_iff]
107:   rintro _ ⟨_, rfl, s, rfl⟩
108:   simp only [IsLocalizedModule.mk'_zero, mem_bot]
109: 
110: @[simp]
111: lemma localized'_bot : (⊥ : Submodule R M).localized' S p f = ⊥ :=
112:   SetLike.ext' (by apply SetLike.ext'_iff.mp <| Submodule.localized₀_bot p f)
113: 
114: @[simp]
115: lemma localized₀_top : (⊤ : Submodule R M).localized₀ p f = ⊤ := by
116:   rw [← top_le_iff]
117:   rintro x _
118:   obtain ⟨⟨x, s⟩, rfl⟩ := IsLocalizedModule.mk'_surjective p f x
119:   exact ⟨x, trivial, s, rfl⟩
120: 
121: @[simp]
122: lemma localized'_top : (⊤ : Submodule R M).localized' S p f = ⊤ :=
123:   SetLike.ext' (by apply SetLike.ext'_iff.mp <| Submodule.localized₀_top p f)
124: 
125: theorem localized₀_inf :
126:     (M' ⊓ M'').localized₀ p f = M'.localized₀ p f ⊓ M''.localized₀ p f := by
127:   simp only [Submodule.ext_iff, Submodule.mem_inf, mem_localized₀]
128:   refine fun x ↦ ⟨by grind, ?_⟩
129:   rintro ⟨⟨i, hi, s, hs⟩, j, hj, t, ht⟩
130:   have h := ht.trans hs.symm
131:   rw [IsLocalizedModule.mk'_eq_mk'_iff] at h
132:   obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := h
133:   refine ⟨(k * t) • i, ⟨M'.smul_of_tower_mem (k * t) hi, ?_⟩, k * s * t, ?_⟩
134:   · rw [mul_smul, hk, smul_smul]
135:     exact M''.smul_of_tower_mem (k * s) hj
136:   · rwa [mul_smul, hk, smul_smul, IsLocalizedModule.mk'_cancel_left]
137: 
138: theorem localized'_inf :
139:     (M' ⊓ M'').localized' S p f = M'.localized' S p f ⊓ M''.localized' S p f :=
140:   SetLike.ext' (by apply SetLike.ext'_iff.mp <| Submodule.localized₀_inf p f M' M'')
141: 
142: theorem localized'_iSup {ι : Type*} (g : ι → Submodule R M) :
143:     (⨆ i, g i).localized' S p f = ⨆ i, (g i).localized' S p f := by
144:   exact GaloisConnection.l_iSup (localized'gi S p f).gc
145: 
146: theorem localized₀_iSup {ι : Type*} (g : ι → Submodule R M) :
147:     (⨆ i, g i).localized₀ p f = ⨆ i, (g i).localized₀ p f := by
148:   let : Module (Localization p) N := IsLocalizedModule.module p f
149:   have : IsScalarTower R (Localization p) N := IsLocalizedModule.isScalarTower_module p f
150:   simpa using! congr_arg (restrictScalars R) (localized'_iSup (Localization p) p f g)

153: noncomputable def localized₀FrameHom : FrameHom (Submodule R M) (Submodule R N) where
154:   toFun := localized₀ p f
155:   map_inf' := localized₀_inf p f
156:   map_top' := localized₀_top p f
157:   map_sSup' s := by rw [sSup_eq_iSup', localized₀_iSup, sSup_image']
158: 
159: @[simp]
160: lemma IsLocalizedModule.localized₀FrameHom_apply :
161:     localized₀FrameHom p f M' = M'.localized₀ p f :=
162:   rfl

164: /-- `localized'` as a `FrameHom`. -/
165: noncomputable def localized'FrameHom :
166:     FrameHom (Submodule R M) (Submodule S N) where
167:   toFun := localized' S p f
168:   map_inf' := localized'_inf S p f

tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

tools.name: request_user_input
tools.description: Request user input for one to three short questions and wait for the response. This tool is only available in Plan mode.

questions.description: Questions to show the user. Prefer 1 and do not exceed 3

header.description: Short header label shown in the UI (12 or fewer chars).

options.description: Provide 2-3 mutually exclusive choices. Put the recommended option first and suffix its label with "(Recommended)". Do not include an "Other" option in this list; the client will add a free-form "Other" option automatically.

description.description: One short sentence explaining impact/tradeoff if selected.

question.description: Single-sentence prompt shown to the user.

tools.name: request_user_input_async
tools.description: Ask the user one or more questions during ongoing work. Use this tool only to request missing information, preferences, constraints, clarification, or approval. The tool returns immediately without ending the turn or waiting for a reply; any reply arrives asynchronously as a new user message. Keep questions concise, self-contained, and easy to understand, using a level of detail appropriate to the user and task. The UI always allows a free-text answer, including when suggested options are provided. A preselected option is not submitted automatically.

questions.description: One or more self-contained questions to present together, in display order.

options.description: Suggested answers, in display order. Put the recommended answer first; the first option is preselected by default. The user can select one option or enter a free-text answer. Do not include an Other option or a free-text placeholder; the UI provides free-text input automatically. Omit options for a free-text-only question.

title.description: The complete question shown to the user, including any context needed to answer it.

tools.name: clock
tools.description: Tools for reading and waiting on time.

tools.name: sleep
tools.description: Pause execution for a specified duration. The sleep ends early when new input arrives for the active turn. Returns the elapsed wall-clock time.

duration_ms.description: How long to sleep in milliseconds. Must be between 1 and 43200000.

tools.name: collaboration

24: theorem isLocalizedModule_iff_isLocalization :
25:     IsLocalizedModule S (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R A Aₛ).toLinearMap ↔
26:       IsLocalization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid A S) Aₛ := by
27:   rw [isLocalizedModule_iff, isLocalization_iff]
28:   refine and_congr ?_ (and_congr (forall_congr' fun _ ↦ ?_) (forall₂_congr fun _ _ ↦ ?_))

30:       Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid, ← SetLike.mem_coe, Submonoid.coe_map,
31:       Set.forall_mem_image, ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply]
32:   · simp_rw [Prod.exists, Subtype.exists, Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid]
33:     simp [← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply, Submonoid.mk_smul, Algebra.smul_def, mul_comm]
34:   · congr!; simp_rw [Subtype.exists, Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid]; simp [Algebra.smul_def]
35: 
36: instance [IsLocalization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid A S) Aₛ] :
37:     IsLocalizedModule S (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R A Aₛ).toLinearMap :=

42: /-- `A` is a localization of a commutative semiring `R` with respect to `S` iff
43: the associated linear map `R →ₗ[R] A` is a localization of modules with respect to `S`. -/
44: lemma isLocalizedModule_iff_isLocalization' :
45:     IsLocalizedModule S (Algebra.linearMap R A) ↔ IsLocalization S A := by
46:   convert! isLocalizedModule_iff_isLocalization (S := S) (A := R) (Aₛ := A)
47:   exact (Submonoid.map_id S).symm

13: # Localization of Submodules
14: 
15: Results about localizations of submodules and quotient modules are provided in this file.
16: 
17: ## Main results
18: - `Submodule.localized`:
19:   The localization of an `R`-submodule of `M` at `p` viewed as an `Rₚ`-submodule of `Mₚ`.
20:   A direct consequence of this is that `Rₚ` is flat over `R`; see `IsLocalization.flat`.
21: - `Submodule.toLocalized`:
22:   The localization map of a submodule `M' →ₗ[R] M'.localized p`.
23: - `Submodule.toLocalizedQuotient`:
24:   The localization map of a quotient module `M ⧸ M' →ₗ[R] LocalizedModule p M ⧸ M'.localized p`.
25: 
26: ## TODO
27: - Statements regarding the exactness of localization.
28: 
29: -/

43: /-- Let `N` be a localization of an `R`-module `M` at `p`.
44: This is the localization of an `R`-submodule of `M` viewed as an `R`-submodule of `N`. -/
45: def localized₀ : Submodule R N where
46:   carrier := { x | ∃ m ∈ M', ∃ s : p, IsLocalizedModule.mk' f m s = x }
47:   add_mem' := fun {x y} ⟨m, hm, s, hx⟩ ⟨n, hn, t, hy⟩ ↦ ⟨t • m + s • n, add_mem (M'.smul_mem t hm)
48:     (M'.smul_mem s hn), s * t, by rw [← hx, ← hy, IsLocalizedModule.mk'_add_mk']⟩
49:   zero_mem' := ⟨0, zero_mem _, 1, by simp⟩
50:   smul_mem' r x := by
51:     rintro ⟨m, hm, s, hx⟩
52:     exact ⟨r • m, smul_mem M' _ hm, s, by rw [IsLocalizedModule.mk'_smul, hx]⟩
53: 
54: /-- Let `S` be the localization of `R` at `p` and `N` be a localization of `M` at `p`.
55: This is the localization of an `R`-submodule of `M` viewed as an `S`-submodule of `N`. -/
56: def localized' : Submodule S N where
57:   __ := localized₀ p f M'
58:   smul_mem' := fun r x ⟨m, hm, s, hx⟩ ↦ by
59:     have ⟨y, t, hyt⟩ := IsLocalization.exists_mk'_eq p r
60:     exact ⟨y • m, M'.smul_mem y hm, t * s, by simp [← hyt, ← hx, IsLocalizedModule.mk'_smul_mk']⟩
61: 
62: lemma mem_localized₀ (x : N) :
63:     x ∈ localized₀ p f M' ↔ ∃ m ∈ M', ∃ s : p, IsLocalizedModule.mk' f m s = x :=
64:   Iff.rfl
65: 
66: lemma mem_localized' (x : N) :
67:     x ∈ localized' S p f M' ↔ ∃ m ∈ M', ∃ s : p, IsLocalizedModule.mk' f m s = x :=
68:   Iff.rfl

71: lemma restrictScalars_localized' :
72:     (localized' S p f M').restrictScalars R = localized₀ p f M' :=
73:   rfl

75: theorem localized'_eq_span : localized' S p f M' = span S (f '' M') := by
76:   refine le_antisymm ?_ (span_le.mpr <| by rintro _ ⟨m, hm, rfl⟩; exact ⟨m, hm, 1, by simp⟩)
77:   rintro _ ⟨m, hm, s, rfl⟩
78:   rw [← one_smul R m, ← mul_one s, ← IsLocalizedModule.mk'_smul_mk' S]
79:   exact smul_mem _ _ (subset_span ⟨m, hm, by simp⟩)

81: theorem map_le_localized₀ : M'.map f ≤ localized₀ p f M' := by
82:   rintro - ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩
83:   rw [mem_localized₀]
84:   exact ⟨x, hx, 1, IsLocalizedModule.mk'_one p f x⟩

87: where `S` is the localization of `R` at `p` and `N` is the localization of `M` at `p`. -/
88: def localized'gi : GaloisInsertion (localized' S p f) (comap f <| ·.restrictScalars R) where
89:   gc M' N' := ⟨fun h m hm ↦ h ⟨m, hm, 1, by simp⟩, fun h ↦ by
90:     rw [localized'_eq_span, span_le]; apply map_le_iff_le_comap.mpr h⟩
91:   le_l_u N' n hn := by
92:     obtain ⟨⟨m, s⟩, rfl⟩ := IsLocalizedModule.mk'_surjective p f n
93:     refine ⟨m, ?_, s, rfl⟩
94:     rw [mem_comap, restrictScalars_mem, ← IsLocalizedModule.mk'_cancel' _ _ s,
95:       Submonoid.smul_def, ← algebraMap_smul S]
96:     exact smul_mem _ _ hn
97:   choice x _ := localized' S p f x
98:   choice_eq _ _ := rfl

126:     (M' ⊓ M'').localized₀ p f = M'.localized₀ p f ⊓ M''.localized₀ p f := by
127:   simp only [Submodule.ext_iff, Submodule.mem_inf, mem_localized₀]
128:   refine fun x ↦ ⟨by grind, ?_⟩
129:   rintro ⟨⟨i, hi, s, hs⟩, j, hj, t, ht⟩

134:   · rw [mul_smul, hk, smul_smul]
135:     exact M''.smul_of_tower_mem (k * s) hj
136:   · rwa [mul_smul, hk, smul_smul, IsLocalizedModule.mk'_cancel_left]

tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.

43: /-- Let `N` be a localization of an `R`-module `M` at `p`.

45: def localized₀ : Submodule R N where
46:   carrier := { x | ∃ m ∈ M', ∃ s : p, IsLocalizedModule.mk' f m s = x }
47:   add_mem' := fun {x y} ⟨m, hm, s, hx⟩ ⟨n, hn, t, hy⟩ ↦ ⟨t • m + s • n, add_mem (M'.smul_mem t hm)
48:     (M'.smul_mem s hn), s * t, by rw [← hx, ← hy, IsLocalizedModule.mk'_add_mk']⟩
49:   zero_mem' := ⟨0, zero_mem _, 1, by simp⟩
50:   smul_mem' r x := by
51:     rintro ⟨m, hm, s, hx⟩

54: /-- Let `S` be the localization of `R` at `p` and `N` be a localization of `M` at `p`.
55: This is the localization of an `R`-submodule of `M` viewed as an `S`-submodule of `N`. -/
56: def localized' : Submodule S N where
57:   __ := localized₀ p f M'
58:   smul_mem' := fun r x ⟨m, hm, s, hx⟩ ↦ by
59:     have ⟨y, t, hyt⟩ := IsLocalization.exists_mk'_eq p r

tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

12: /-!
13: # Localization of Submodules
14: 
15: Results about localizations of submodules and quotient modules are provided in this file.
16: 
17: ## Main results
18: - `Submodule.localized`:
19:   The localization of an `R`-submodule of `M` at `p` viewed as an `Rₚ`-submodule of `Mₚ`.
20:   A direct consequence of this is that `Rₚ` is flat over `R`; see `IsLocalization.flat`.
21: - `Submodule.toLocalized`:
22:   The localization map of a submodule `M' →ₗ[R] M'.localized p`.
23: - `Submodule.toLocalizedQuotient`:
24:   The localization map of a quotient module `M ⧸ M' →ₗ[R] LocalizedModule p M ⧸ M'.localized p`.
25: 
26: ## TODO
27: - Statements regarding the exactness of localization.
28: 
29: -/

34: 
35: variable {R S M N : Type*}
36: variable (S) [CommSemiring R] [CommSemiring S] [AddCommMonoid M] [AddCommMonoid N]
37: variable [Module R M] [Module R N] [Algebra R S] [Module S N] [IsScalarTower R S N]
38: variable (p : Submonoid R) [IsLocalization p S] (f : M →ₗ[R] N) [IsLocalizedModule p f]
39: variable (M' M'' : Submodule R M)
40: 
41: namespace Submodule
42: 
43: /-- Let `N` be a localization of an `R`-module `M` at `p`.
44: This is the localization of an `R`-submodule of `M` viewed as an `R`-submodule of `N`. -/
45: def localized₀ : Submodule R N where
46:   carrier := { x | ∃ m ∈ M', ∃ s : p, IsLocalizedModule.mk' f m s = x }
47:   add_mem' := fun {x y} ⟨m, hm, s, hx⟩ ⟨n, hn, t, hy⟩ ↦ ⟨t • m + s • n, add_mem (M'.smul_mem t hm)
48:     (M'.smul_mem s hn), s * t, by rw [← hx, ← hy, IsLocalizedModule.mk'_add_mk']⟩
49:   zero_mem' := ⟨0, zero_mem _, 1, by simp⟩
50:   smul_mem' r x := by
51:     rintro ⟨m, hm, s, hx⟩
52:     exact ⟨r • m, smul_mem M' _ hm, s, by rw [IsLocalizedModule.mk'_smul, hx]⟩
53: 
54: /-- Let `S` be the localization of `R` at `p` and `N` be a localization of `M` at `p`.
55: This is the localization of an `R`-submodule of `M` viewed as an `S`-submodule of `N`. -/
56: def localized' : Submodule S N where
57:   __ := localized₀ p f M'

tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

11: /-!
12: # Equivalence between `IsLocalizedModule` and `IsLocalization`
13: -/
14: 
15: public section
16: 
17: section IsLocalizedModule
18: 
19: variable {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] (S : Submonoid R)
20: variable {A Aₛ : Type*} [CommSemiring A] [Algebra R A]
21: variable [CommSemiring Aₛ] [Algebra A Aₛ] [Algebra R Aₛ] [IsScalarTower R A Aₛ]
22: 
23: variable {S} in
24: theorem isLocalizedModule_iff_isLocalization :
25:     IsLocalizedModule S (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R A Aₛ).toLinearMap ↔
26:       IsLocalization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid A S) Aₛ := by
27:   rw [isLocalizedModule_iff, isLocalization_iff]
28:   refine and_congr ?_ (and_congr (forall_congr' fun _ ↦ ?_) (forall₂_congr fun _ _ ↦ ?_))
29:   · simp_rw [← (Algebra.lmul R Aₛ).commutes, Algebra.lmul_isUnit_iff, Subtype.forall,
30:       Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid, ← SetLike.mem_coe, Submonoid.coe_map,
31:       Set.forall_mem_image, ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply]
32:   · simp_rw [Prod.exists, Subtype.exists, Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid]
33:     simp [← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply, Submonoid.mk_smul, Algebra.smul_def, mul_comm]
34:   · congr!; simp_rw [Subtype.exists, Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid]; simp [Algebra.smul_def]
35: 
36: instance [IsLocalization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid A S) Aₛ] :
37:     IsLocalizedModule S (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R A Aₛ).toLinearMap :=
38:   isLocalizedModule_iff_isLocalization.mpr ‹_›
39: 
40: variable (A)
41: 
42: /-- `A` is a localization of a commutative semiring `R` with respect to `S` iff
43: the associated linear map `R →ₗ[R] A` is a localization of modules with respect to `S`. -/
44: lemma isLocalizedModule_iff_isLocalization' :
45:     IsLocalizedModule S (Algebra.linearMap R A) ↔ IsLocalization S A := by
46:   convert! isLocalizedModule_iff_isLocalization (S := S) (A := R) (Aₛ := A)
47:   exact (Submonoid.map_id S).symm
48: 
49: instance [IsLocalization S A] : IsLocalizedModule S (Algebra.linearMap R A) :=
50:   (isLocalizedModule_iff_isLocalization' S _).mpr inferInstance
51: 
52: variable {S A} in
53: /-- `IsLocalization.mk'` agrees with `IsLocalizedModule.mk'`. -/
54: lemma IsLocalization.mk'_algebraMap_eq_mk' [IsLocalization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid A S) Aₛ]
55:     {x : A} {s : S} : IsLocalization.mk' Aₛ x ⟨_, Algebra.mem_algebraMapSubmonoid_of_mem s⟩ =
56:       IsLocalizedModule.mk' (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R A Aₛ).toLinearMap x s := by
57:   rw [← IsLocalizedModule.smul_inj (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R A Aₛ).toLinearMap s,
58:     IsLocalizedModule.mk'_cancel', Submonoid.smul_def, ← algebraMap_smul A]
59:   exact IsLocalization.smul_mk'_self (m := ⟨_, _⟩)
60: 
61: /-- `IsLocalization.mk'` agrees with `IsLocalizedModule.mk'`. -/
62: lemma IsLocalization.mk'_eq_mk' [IsLocalization S A] (x : R) (s : S) :
63:     IsLocalization.mk' A x s = IsLocalizedModule.mk' (Algebra.linearMap R A) x s := by
64:   rw [← IsLocalizedModule.smul_inj (Algebra.linearMap R A) s, IsLocalizedModule.mk'_cancel']
65:   exact IsLocalization.smul_mk'_self
66: 
67: end IsLocalizedModule"}

15: Results about localizations of submodules and quotient modules are provided in this file.

17: ## Main results

43: /-- Let `N` be a localization of an `R`-module `M` at `p`.
44: This is the localization of an `R`-submodule of `M` viewed as an `R`-submodule of `N`. -/
45: def localized₀ : Submodule R N where
46:   carrier := { x | ∃ m ∈ M', ∃ s : p, IsLocalizedModule.mk' f m s = x }
47:   add_mem' := fun {x y} ⟨m, hm, s, hx⟩ ⟨n, hn, t, hy⟩ ↦ ⟨t • m + s • n, add_mem (M'.smul_mem t hm)
48:     (M'.smul_mem s hn), s * t, by rw [← hx, ← hy, IsLocalizedModule.mk'_add_mk']⟩
49:   zero_mem' := ⟨0, zero_mem _, 1, by simp⟩
50:   smul_mem' r x := by
51:     rintro ⟨m, hm, s, hx⟩
52:     exact ⟨r • m, smul_mem M' _ hm, s, by rw [IsLocalizedModule.mk'_smul, hx]⟩
53: 
54: /-- Let `S` be the localization of `R` at `p` and `N` be a localization of `M` at `p`.
55: This is the localization of an `R`-submodule of `M` viewed as an `S`-submodule of `N`. -/
56: def localized' : Submodule S N where
57:   __ := localized₀ p f M'
58:   smul_mem' := fun r x ⟨m, hm, s, hx⟩ ↦ by
59:     have ⟨y, t, hyt⟩ := IsLocalization.exists_mk'_eq p r
60:     exact ⟨y • m, M'.smul_mem y hm, t * s, by simp [← hyt, ← hx, IsLocalizedModule.mk'_smul_mk']⟩

62: lemma mem_localized₀ (x : N) :
63:     x ∈ localized₀ p f M' ↔ ∃ m ∈ M', ∃ s : p, IsLocalizedModule.mk' f m s = x :=
64:   Iff.rfl

66: lemma mem_localized' (x : N) :
67:     x ∈ localized' S p f M' ↔ ∃ m ∈ M', ∃ s : p, IsLocalizedModule.mk' f m s = x :=

75: theorem localized'_eq_span : localized' S p f M' = span S (f '' M') := by
76:   refine le_antisymm ?_ (span_le.mpr <| by rintro _ ⟨m, hm, rfl⟩; exact ⟨m, hm, 1, by simp⟩)
77:   rintro _ ⟨m, hm, s, rfl⟩

79:   exact smul_mem _ _ (subset_span ⟨m, hm, by simp⟩)

82:   rintro - ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩
83:   rw [mem_localized₀]
84:   exact ⟨x, hx, 1, IsLocalizedModule.mk'_one p f x⟩

88: def localized'gi : GaloisInsertion (localized' S p f) (comap f <| ·.restrictScalars R) where
89:   gc M' N' := ⟨fun h m hm ↦ h ⟨m, hm, 1, by simp⟩, fun h ↦ by

91:   le_l_u N' n hn := by

93:     refine ⟨m, ?_, s, rfl⟩
94:     rw [mem_comap, restrictScalars_mem, ← IsLocalizedModule.mk'_cancel' _ _ s,

134:   · rw [mul_smul, hk, smul_smul]

tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

The UI always allows a free-text answer, including when suggested options are provided. A preselected option is not submitted automatically.

tools.description:

The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

At the start of your turn, you are the active agent.
You can spawn sub-agents to handle subtasks, and those sub-agents can spawn their own sub-agents.
All agents in the team, including the agents that you can assign tasks to, are equally intelligent and capable, and have access to the same set of tools.

You can use `spawn_agent` to create a new agent, `followup_task` to give an existing agent a new task and trigger a turn, and `send_message` to pass a message to a running agent without triggering a turn.
`send_message` calls may be read by a human, so ensure they are legible. Always put proper spaces between words and/or numbers.
Child agents can also spawn their own sub-agents.
You can decide how much context you want to propagate to your sub-agents with the `fork_turns` parameter.

Message Type: MESSAGE | FINAL_ANSWER

All agents share the same directory. In detail:

When calling `wait_agent`, prefer longer waits (minutes) to avoid busy polling.

There are 4 available concurrency slots, meaning that up to 4 agents can be active at once, including you.

Full-history forks (`fork_turns` omitted or `"all"`) inherit the parent model and reasoning effort and do not accept overrides. 15: Results about localizations of submodules and quotient modules are provided in this file.

19:   The localization of an `R`-submodule of `M` at `p` viewed as an `Rₚ`-submodule of `Mₚ`.

43: /-- Let `N` be a localization of an `R`-module `M` at `p`.

46:   carrier := { x | ∃ m ∈ M', ∃ s : p, IsLocalizedModule.mk' f m s = x }
47:   add_mem' := fun {x y} ⟨m, hm, s, hx⟩ ⟨n, hn, t, hy⟩ ↦ ⟨t • m + s • n, add_mem (M'.smul_mem t hm)
48:     (M'.smul_mem s hn), s * t, by rw [← hx, ← hy, IsLocalizedModule.mk'_add_mk']⟩
49:   zero_mem' := ⟨0, zero_mem _, 1, by simp⟩
50:   smul_mem' r x := by
51:     rintro ⟨m, hm, s, hx⟩

54: /-- Let `S` be the localization of `R` at `p` and `N` be a localization of `M` at `p`.
55: This is the localization of an `R`-submodule of `M` viewed as an `S`-submodule of `N`. -/

59:     have ⟨y, t, hyt⟩ := IsLocalization.exists_mk'_eq p r
60:     exact ⟨y • m, M'.smul_mem y hm, t * s, by simp [← hyt, ← hx, IsLocalizedModule.mk'_smul_mk']⟩
